text:
Michael Rasmussen sat out the Red Wings' game in Florida last week as a healthy scratch, and the numbers explain why it happened and why it might be a little unfair. He has one goal and four points in 20 games, nothing in his last ten, and his ice time has slid to 14:16 a night in that stretch from a season average near 15:30.

The case for patience: he has one goal on 4.21 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a 3.3% shooting rate, and Detroit has scored 10.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league. At five-on-five the Wings get 52% of the expected goals in his minutes, which isn't the profile of a player getting caved in. The case against: even with normal luck, he was never a scorer (14 points in 64 games last season), Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in 2025-26, and his comparables are penalty killers and shot blockers. His value lives in the role, the 6'6" frame, the 29 blocked shots. Whether Detroit still has a lineup spot for that role is the thing to watch.
